r: **Guru Gobind Singh** (1666-1708) = **tenth and last human Guru** of the Sikhs
**Born 1666 at Patna** (Bihar) – Takht Sri Patna Sahib marks the birthplace

**Founded the Khalsa** ("army of the pure") on **Baisakhi, 13 April 1699**, at **Anandpur** (Takht Sri **Keshgarh Sahib**, Rupnagar); the **Panj Pyare** (five volunteers) were baptised first with sacred nectar
He **turned the Sikhs into a military order** (Khalsa; surnames **Singh / Kaur**); the Sikh state was founded by Banda Bahadur (1710)
The **Zafarnama** (Persian letter to Aurangzeb accusing the Mughals of betrayal); Dasam Granth at **Paonta Sahib**
The 40 liberated ones who died defending him at **Muktsar** (Maghi)
Fought Aurangzeb from 1699; made peace with **Bahadur Shah**; killed at **Nanded** (1708)
Declared the **Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru** – personal Guruship ended
The PM attended the celebrations at **Patna** (Gandhi Maidan) on **5 January 2017** and released a stamp

0.x: Gobind Singh: Patna 1666 → Khalsa, Anandpur, Baisakhi 1699 → Nanded 1708; 10th and last Guru.

r: **Maha (Mahan) Singh**, chief of the **Sukerchakia misl**; died when Ranjit Singh was a boy
Of Afghanistan; invaded Punjab (1798); Ranjit Singh returned his cannons lost in the Jhelum, and in **1799 Zaman Shah made him governor of Lahore with the title "Raja"**
**1799: captured Lahore** → **political capital Lahore**, **religious capital Amritsar** (Amritsar taken 1802/1805)
On European lines (**Allard**, Ventura; **Fauj-i-Khas**); commander **Hari Singh Nalwa**
Lord **Minto**; negotiated by **Charles Metcalfe**: **Sutlej** = boundary; Ranjit Singh gave up the cis-Sutlej states and turned west
**1813:** got the **Kohinoor** from **Shah Shuja** (Nadir Shah had taken it from Delhi in 1739)
Covered the Harmandir Sahib in gold → "Golden Temple"

1.x: **Secular ruler:** Hindu and Muslim ministers; blind in one eye – "**God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye, that is why He took away the light from the other**" = **Ranjit Singh**.
Sukerchakia → Lahore 1799 (Zaman Shah's "Raja") → Amritsar treaty 1809 (Sutlej) → Kohinoor 1813 → Kashmir 1819 → died 1839.

r: Friendly – grant of about **500 bighas** of land where Ramdaspur (Amritsar) grew
**Executed 1606** for helping rebel Prince **Khusrau** – **first martyr Guru**
Held in **Gwalior Fort**, freed 1619 (with 52 prisoners – Bandi Chhor Divas); only imprisoned
**Publicly executed at Delhi (Chandni Chowk), 1675**, for refusing Islam – "**Hind-di-Chadar**"
Wars from 1699; Zafarnama; later peace with Bahadur Shah

2.x: **Sikh Guru executed by Aurangzeb = Tegh Bahadur**.
**Gurus put to death by the rulers = Arjan Dev (1606) and Tegh Bahadur (1675)**; Angad was not, and Hargobind was only imprisoned.
**Sis Ganj** = place of Tegh Bahadur's execution; **Rakab Ganj** = his cremation; the 350th martyrdom year was observed in 2025-26.
Akbar–Ram Das (land); Jahangir–Arjan (1606) and Hargobind (Gwalior); Aurangzeb–Tegh Bahadur (1675).

3.x: Ranjit Singh died **June 1839** → disputed successions: **Kharak (Khadag) Singh (1839, immediate successor)** → Nau Nihal Singh → Sher Singh → **Duleep (Dalip) Singh (1843)**; **Hari Singh Nalwa** was a general, not a successor.
**Duleep Singh** = youngest son, crowned at five (1843) with his mother **Rani Jindan (Jind Kaur)** as regent = **last king of the Sikh empire (1843-1849)**.

r: **Went to Russia** seeking Tsar Alexander III's help
**Died in Paris, October 1893** (22 Oct in most references; 23 Oct in some); **buried with Christian rites at Elveden, England**

3.x: Kharak Singh first, Duleep Singh last; Duleep: Christian 1853 → Sikh 1886 → Russia 1887 → died Paris 1893, buried Elveden.

r: (**1469-1539**) = **founder of Sikhism**; born at **Talwandi = Nankana (Sahib)** near the Ravi (now Pakistan)
One formless God (**Ik Onkar**), **Naam Simran**, **Sangat**, **Langar**, honest householder life; against idol worship and rituals of both faiths
**Successor = Bhai Lehna → Guru Angad**, appointed by Nanak before his death (1539)
Founded **Ramdaspur (Amritsar)**; land from Akbar; holy tank
Compiled **Adi Granth (1604)**; built **Harmandir Sahib**; first martyr
Militarised the Panth; **Miri-Piri**; **Akal Takht** (1609); Gwalior Fort; battle of Kartarpur
Born **Tyag Mal**; founded **Anandpur Sahib (Chak Nanki)**; 116 hymns; executed 1675
Born Patna 1666; **Khalsa 1699**; Five Ks; Guruship to the Granth

4.x: Sikh = disciple; Nanak (Talwandi 1469) → Angad (Gurmukhi) → Amar Das (Manjis) → Ram Das (Amritsar) → Arjan (Adi Granth).

r: City and tank founded by **Guru Ram Das** on land granted by Akbar
Built / completed by **Guru Arjan Dev** (1604), who installed the Adi Granth; gold covering by Ranjit Singh
Founded by Tegh Bahadur; Khalsa born here 1699 (Keshgarh Sahib); **Hola Mohalla**
Final version of the Guru Granth Sahib (1705); Baisakhi fair
**Death / cremation place of Guru Gobind Singh (1708)**, stabbed there by an Afghan – Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib

5.x: **Amritsar was established by Guru Ram Das**; the **Golden Temple was completed by Guru Arjan Dev**; **Nanded is sacred because of Guru Gobind Singh**.
Ram Das = city; Arjan = temple; Hargobind = Akal Takht; Nanded = Gobind Singh's samadhi.

6.x: **Original name Lachhman Dev**; Guru Gobind Singh named him **Banda** and sent him north from **Nanded (1708)**.

r: Defeated **Wazir Khan** at **Chappar Chiri**; conquered **Sirhind** → **first sovereign Sikh state**, capital **Lohgarh** (Sirhind Fateh Diwas, 12-14 May)
Eight-month siege of **Gurdas Nangal**; captured by **Farrukhsiyar's** forces
**Executed at Delhi** by **Farrukhsiyar** for refusing to convert

6.x: Abolished zamindari and gave farmers ownership of land; struck **coins in the names of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh**.
Bandai and Tat Khalsa split (healed 1721, Bhai Mani Singh); **Dal Khalsa** (Kapur Singh) = combined force; Khalsa rule between the **Sutlej and Jamuna**.
**12 misls** (misl = "equal"; democratic military brotherhoods): **Bhangi, Ahluwalia, Ramgarhia, Kanhaiya, Sukerchakia, Phulkian** …; the Kanphata were Nath yogis, not a misl.
Banda: Lachhman Dev → Sirhind 1710 (Lohgarh) → executed 1716 by Farrukhsiyar; 12 misls → Ranjit Singh (Sukerchakia).

r: **Adi Granth compiled by Guru Arjan (5th) in 1604**
**By Guru Gobind Singh at Damdama Sahib (1705)**
Script **Gurmukhi**; language "Sant Bhasha" (a mix of Punjabi, Hindi and dialects)
Hymns of six Gurus (incl. **116 hymns of Tegh Bahadur**) and of non-Sikh saints: **Kabir**, Sufi **Sheikh (Baba) Farid**, **Namdev**, **Ravidas** (**41 shabdas**), Jaidev
Sikh marriage **Anand Karaj** = four circumambulations of the Granth while **Lavan** hymns are sung

7.x: Arjan 1604 (Adi Granth) → Gobind Singh 1705 (final) → eternal Guru 1708.
